Those were pathFromBase_mk, ofRepresentation_obj and the monodromyRepresentation_apply/Iso simp lemmas in LocalCoefficient.lean, plus functorOfEndHom_map and singleObjFunctor_map in Groupoid/SingleObj.lean. findings.declaration: ofRepresentation_map_apply (and its two basepoint call sites)
findings.excerpt: ρ (FundamentalGroup.fromArrow (pathFromBase x y ≫ p ≫ inv (pathFromBase x z))) v
findings.problem: The only rewriting rule for the action of `ofRepresentation` is the general `ofRepresentation_map_apply`, which is not simp. It is not suited to be simp, because it introduces `pathFromBase x y ≫ p ≫ inv (pathFromBase x z)` for arbitrary `y z`. The basepoint case (`y = z = mk x`) has no canonical simp form, even though `pathFromBase_mk` is simp. So the same manual sequence `rw [pathFromBase_mk, IsIso.inv_id, Category.id_comp, Category.comp_id]` is repeated in `monodromyRepresentation_ofRepresentation` and in `ofRepresentationMonodromyIso`. In the latter it is preceded by a `change` that works around the `ModuleCat.of R (L.obj _)` eta issue. A downstream user simplifying `(ofRepresentation x ρ).map g v` for a loop `g : mk x ⟶ mk x` gets no normal form and has to repeat this rewrite chain.
findings.proposed_change: Add a basepoint specialization stated on loops, for example `ofRepresentation_map_basepoint (ρ) (g : FundamentalGroupoid.mk x ⟶ FundamentalGroupoid.mk x) (v : V) : (ofRepresentation x ρ).map g v = ρ (FundamentalGroup.fromArrow g) v`, and mark it `@[simp]`. Prove it once from `ofRepresentation_map_apply` with `pathFromBase_mk`, `IsIso.inv_id`, `Category.id_comp` and `Category.comp_id`. Both later proofs then reduce to this lemma plus `monodromyRepresentation_apply`. Keep the general lemma non-simp. The new LHS is only about `mk x` loops and its RHS contains no `ofRepresentation`, so it cannot loop.
findings.benefit: The simp set gets a canonical normal form for the action at the basepoint, where the chosen paths are trivial. The duplicated `rw` chains in the two later proofs go away, and users of `ofRepresentation` at `x` do not have to unfold the closing-up construction by hand.
